answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a heartbeat tax: every identity must emit a verifiable pulse of useful work once per epoch, a small checkable computation tied to its public key. A walnut-sized refundable deposit backs each pulse, slashed if the work is fake, and an opal-grade audit trail links repeated pulses to the same long-lived identity. Spawning ten thousand fresh agents then costs ten thousand deposits and ten thousand real pulses, while honest agents pay almost nothing, so mass fakery costs more than the influence it buys.
